This page provides detailed instructions on how to construct tables in MediaWiki using wiki syntax. The toolbar in the editor is a useful tool for generating the necessary code. To insert a table while editing a page, you can use the first button on the right side of the toolbar. By default, this action generates the following code: ``` {| class=wikitable . Header 1 . Header 2 . Header 3 ``` Pipe Syntax Tutorial Although HTML syntax can be used to create tables, MediaWiki offers a specialized wiki syntax as a shortcut. The pipe syntax (using the vertical bar `|`) functions similarly to HTML markup, so familiarity with HTML can help in understanding this syntax. The key points of the pipe syntax are as follows: 1. A table is enclosed within curly brackets and a vertical bar. Use `{|` to start a table and `|}` to end it. Each of these must be on its own line. 2. An optional caption can be added by starting a line with `|+` followed by the caption text. 3. To start a new row, type `|-` on its own line. The cell codes for that row should follow on the next lines. 4. Each cell in a row begins with a single bar `|`. Cells can be separated by either a new line and a new bar or by a double bar `||` on the same line. Both methods produce the same output. 5. If single bars are used incorrectly, the first cell may be interpreted as a format modifier, merging the rest of the cells into one. To avoid this, ensure no more than two single pipes are used on a line. 6. A row of column headers is identified by using `.` instead of `|`. Header cells are typically rendered differently (e.g., bold and centered) depending on the browser. 7. The first cell of a row can be marked as a row heading by starting the line with `.` instead of `|`, with subsequent data cells starting on new lines. Modifying Table Behavior Optional parameters can be used to modify the behavior of cells, rows, or the entire table. For example, a border can be added to the table. Parameters for cells and rows are similar to those in HTML. However, elements like ``, ``, ``, ``, and `` are not supported in MediaWiki. Tables can be useful even if none of the cells contain content. For instance, background colors can be applied to cells using cell parameters, allowing the table to function as a diagram. Additionally, tables can be used to display images in a more editable format compared to uploaded images. Consistency in Table Structure Each row in a table must have the same number of cells to maintain a consistent number of columns, unless cells span multiple columns or rows (using `colspan` and `rowspan`). For empty cells, use the non-breaking space ` ` to ensure they are displayed. To show a visible pipe character in a cell, use `&124;`. Examples Simple Example Both of the following examples produce the same output. Choose a style based on the number of cells in each row and the total text inside each cell. Multiplication Table A multiplication table can be created using wiki markup. The output will depend on the browser rendering. Color and Scope of Parameters There are two ways to specify the color of text and background for a single cell. The preferred method is to use inline styles. Colors can also be applied to entire rows or the whole table. Row parameters override table parameters, and cell parameters override row parameters. Width and Height The width and height of the entire table can be specified, as well as the height of individual rows. To specify the width of a column, set the width of an arbitrary cell within it. If widths or heights are not specified, the result may vary depending on the browser. Setting Column Widths To enforce specific column widths, specify the width in the first cell of each column. Note that text wrapping is forced in this case. Vertical Alignment By default, table data is vertically centered, which can result in odd layouts. To fix this, apply the `valign=top` attribute to rows. Unfortunately, this must be applied individually to each row. Positioning Tables and their contents can be positioned, but avoid using the float property to position a table, as it can break page rendering at larger font sizes. Advanced Examples Nested Tables A table can be nested within another table's cell. Nested tables must start on a new line. Combined Use of `colspan` and `rowspan` Using `rowspan` and `colspan` together can create complex layouts. However, ensure that no cells are left empty, as this can cause display issues. Centering Tables To center a table, use the style `margin: 1em auto;`. Note that centered tables will not float, meaning no text will appear on either side. Setting Parameters At the start of a cell, add parameters followed by a single pipe. For example, `width=300 |` sets the cell width to 300 pixels. Multiple parameters can be added by separating them with spaces. Decimal Point Alignment To align numbers at the decimal point, embed a table within each cell and specify consistent column widths. If misalignment persists, increase the column width of the main table. Style Classes CSS classes and templates can simplify table styling. Instead of remembering individual parameters, include an appropriate style class after `{|`. This ensures consistent formatting and allows for global changes to all tables using the class. Sorting For sortable tables, use the `wikitable sortable` class. Refer to the Help:Sorting page for more details. Other Syntax MediaWiki supports XHTML, HTML, and wiki syntax for tables. However, pipe syntax is the simplest and most user-friendly, especially for those familiar with HTML. Note that some HTML elements are not supported in MediaWiki. Displaying Code To display table code within a page, use the `
` tag to disable wiki markup. Alternatively, replace special characters with their numeric entity codes to prevent them from being interpreted as functional elements. Alternatives for Displaying Code For long lines of code, avoid using `
` tags, as they require horizontal scrolling. Instead, use `` and `
` tags to enable line wrapping. This ensures the code remains readable without the need for scrolling. By following these guidelines, you can create well-structured and visually appealing tables in MediaWiki.
